card.band: 8 h. Semantics-preserving versions are within reach. Byte-exact output needs the same rewrite order, which is hard, so the average sits below the reference. A weaker model breaks the build or the behaviour. Buckets: one per pass.
card.cheat: Making passes no-ops preserves behaviour but fails the text comparison. Upstream pass sources are absent, and binaryen is not installed in the image.
card.grading: wasm-opt runs each pass on hidden .wast inputs from the lit suite plus fuzz-generated modules. Output text is compared against a sealed upstream build, and wasm-opt --fuzz-exec (or wasm-interp) must show unchanged behaviour. Score is the fraction of cases with identical output, with a smaller weight for semantically equal but different output. The base fails all of them.
card.reference: The original pass sources, several thousand lines of C++. They score 1.
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot where five function-level passes are removed: vacuum, remove-unused-brs, simplify-locals, merge-blocks and dce. The agent re-implements them against the IR and pass-runner API, registers them with wasm-opt, and the project builds with cmake.

v1.kill_reason: Grading demands byte-identical text to the sealed upstream build, so a different valid re-implementation earns only the small semantic-equal weight. No realistic trial reaches 0.9 of reference, and the only route to high credit is reproducing the public upstream sources. Rescope to semantics plus size or structure checks to revive it.

Band.why: Byte-exact output to upstream means only near-recall of upstream passes can reach 0.9 of reference; no dated evidence; weaker-model lag unverified.

Build.why: Build est. under 1 h but grader setup with sealed upstream outputs and lit harness is multi-day.

Fit.why: CPU-only cmake build fits the sandbox.

Hor.why: Five passes with interactions fit an 8 h tier, though a byte-exact target caps the reachable work.

Lic.why: Apache-2.0 allows shipping the snapshot and reference.

Multi.why: One bucket per pass gives steady partial credit, but the exact-text weighting is not steady across buckets.

Nov.why: Nearest neighbour 0.25 (S-im-065) is above 0.15; not crowded.

Real.why: Public tag, Apache-2.0, real project with lit suite; seed filenames and pass set need correction (CamelCase files).

Ref.why: Complete permissive upstream implementation at the pinned tag would score exactly 1.

Seal.why: Snapshot removes the sources offline, but the public tag and its test expectations let a model reconstruct the code.

Surf.why: Lit suite plus unlimited fuzz-generated modules gives a large executable surface.

spike_plan.kill_if: Output differs between two builds of the same tag, or the exact-text target can only be met by copying upstream.
spike_plan.pass_if: Two builds give identical output on sampled inputs, the five files total 2000+ lines, and a semantics-only check gives a graded curve.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone WebAssembly/binaryen at version_133 and build with cmake (Release, -j8); record wall time and whether the suite runs.

Pick 5 lit .wast files each for dce, vacuum, remove-unused-brs, simplify-locals, merge-blocks from test/passes and run wasm-opt --<pass> on them twice in separate build dirs to check byte-identical output.
Delete the five pass sources in a copy, stub them to no-ops, and confirm the text comparison fails on the sampled files (validates that exact-text scoring is what separates solutions).
Run --fuzz-exec on 20 generated modules with the reference build to confirm behaviour checks are deterministic.
Count the lines of the five upstream pass files to replace the 'several thousand' estimate.
Ask: does a semantics-only variant (fuzz-exec equivalence plus size no worse than upstream) give a usable partial-credit curve? If yes, rescope the grading to it.

v1.summary: Binaryen version_133 is real and Apache-2.0, and its pass sources are public, so the reference is strong but the file names in the seed are wrong (upstream uses CamelCase). The card fails because grading requires byte-exact output matching upstream, which encodes the reference's internal rewrite order and lets only recall reach high scores; killed K9 with a suggested semantics-first rescope.
